extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users (mathematicians, authors preparing mathematical documents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and feature-summary for using AMS-LaTeX to typeset mathematical documents: multi-line equations, theorem environments, document classes, and symbol fonts; includes usage examples (amsmath, align, theorem, proof).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typesetting multi-line equations
rubrics_metrics.description: The package has a suite of facilities to format multi-line equations. For example, the align environment causes alignment of relation symbols (equals signs) across lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from page: use \usepackage{amsmath} and then \begin{align} y&=(x+1)^2 \\ & = x^2+2x+1 \end{align} — this causes the equals signs in the two lines to be aligned with one another. Use align (and other amsmath environments) for multi-line displayed math rather than manual spacing or separate displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and numbering theorems, lemmas, etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS-LaTeX includes flexible commands/environments for formatting and numbering theorems, lemmas, and similar structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from page: one may use the environment \begin{theorem}[Pythagoras] ... \end{theorem} and \begin{proof} ... \end{proof} to generate a numbered Theorem (with optional name) and an associated proof (ending with □). Prefer these environments to ad-hoc bold/italic headings so numbering, cross-referencing, and consistent styling are automatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document classes and packages for mathematical documents
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS-LaTeX is a collection of LaTeX document classes and packages developed for the American Mathematical Society; it provides document-class-level support tailored to mathematical publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical usage shown: \documentclass{article} plus \usepackage{amsmath} (and related AMS packages). Use the AMS-provided classes/packages when preparing mathematical articles to get AMS-consistent formatting and features (rather than plain article with manual macros).

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS fonts and comprehensive mathematical symbol support
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS-LaTeX additions include fonts containing numerous mathematical symbols (AMSFonts) to support advanced mathematical typesetting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes AMSFonts (v3.0) as part of the AMS-LaTeX suite. When requiring additional symbols beyond base LaTeX, load AMS fonts/packages provided by AMS-LaTeX rather than inventing custom glyphs; ensures consistent metric and stylistic behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web rendering compatibility via MathJax
rubrics_metrics.description: MathJax supports AMS-LaTeX through extensions, allowing AMS-LaTeX syntax to be rendered in web contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If producing web-hosted mathematics (e.g., blogs, wikis), use AMS-LaTeX-compatible syntax and rely on MathJax extensions for client-side rendering. This preserves AMS environments (align, theorem, etc.) in web output.
